title: Tune NCCL overlap scheduling and KV-cache continuous batching for tensor-parallel
author: Arjun Patel
description: Context: Tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads at scale see stalls where NCCL collectives and device kernels end up serialized due to stream scheduling and sync points. These stalls increase p99 latency and reduce steady-state throughput for long-context workloads that rely on KV cache and continuous batching. Motivation: Reduce comm/compute stalls by (1) introducing a lightweight NCCL/stream scheduling layer that prioritizes comm streams and defers kernel launches until comms reach safe points, (2) moving kernel syncs off the hot path using CUDA events and asynchronous checks, and (3) reworking the KV-cache continuous batching logic to better compact requests and avoid micro-bursts that hurt overlap. Summary of changes: - add src/runtime/nccl_scheduler.cpp/h: implements prioritized stream selection, async event barriers and NCCL-launch helpers - tune stream priorities and affinity for common NVLink topologies - refactor src/runtime/kvcache.cpp to implement continuous-batch coalescing, backpressure thresholds and a lightweight batching window - add a per-request tracing metric for comm/compute overlap and KV-cache spill events - update perf harness tests and add an end-to-end benchmark (tests/perf/tp_overlap_bench.py) - add CI/benchmark gating to detect regressions on 4/8 GPU configs Results: In our internal perf runs (8xA100, sequence lengths 768/2048, model: 70B TP=8) we measured: - throughput +22% (seq=2048), +18% (seq=768) - p50 token latency -12%, p99 -18% - KV-cache spill rate down ~40% for heavy continuous-batching patterns - no regression on single-GPU fallback Safety and rollout: Changes are gated by a feature flag (runtime.tuning.tp_overlap = true). The default remains current scheduling. The PR includes rollout docs and a Canary plan (canary on Dedicated clusters with 50% traffic and traffic shadowing). CI: initial perf-check detected a transient regression in an integration test; addressed by reducing a small race in the scheduler (see commits). Backwards compatibility: no API changes; purely runtime optimizations.
